sampling.method: d3_resolve objects have no own `id` field, so each pair's was given a synthetic id `<pairId>-D3-resolve` (e.g. `DIFF-01-D3-resolve`) for ordinal sorting and shuffling purposes only (not written back into d3_resolve). All 214 ids (208 real + 6 synthetic) were sorted with C `string.CompareOrdinal` (byte-value ordinal), then shuffled with a small .NET 10 console program implementing Fisher-Yates exactly as benchmarks/corpora/tools/CorpusSyntaxTool/Program.cs:577-583 does it (`var random = new Random(20260920); for (int i = array.Length-1; i > 0; i--) { int j = random.Next(0, i+1); swap(array[i], array[j]); }`), then the first `max(10, ceil(0.25*214))=54` of the shuffled order were kept. Program source and full 214-id shuffled output saved under the task scratchpad (`...\scratchpad\task027-crosscheck-litedb\Sampler.cs`, `all_ids.txt`, `shuffled_all.txt`, `sample_ids.txt`) for reproducibility; not committed to the repo.

crossCheckPlan.verificationMethod: For every sampled `id`, read the exact stated `path`/`line` (or `startLine..endLine`) directly from `git show <commit>:<path>` at the corpus clone D:\worktrees\corpus\medium-litedb (pinned commit confirmed via `git rev-parse HEAD`, clean working tree, `core.autocrlf=false`), independent of this file's own text and of any CV/runner output. Checked: the stated line's actual content matches the claimed symbol/kind; for N3 entries, the receiver's declared/inferred type (re-derived from the enclosing method, matching CONVENTIONS.md's N3 rule) matches the claimed `receiverType`; for D2Excluded flags, `git diff --numstat` between `c` and `cPrime` for the entry's file was independently re-run and compared to the `p`->`cPrime` numstat. Additionally (leader instruction, full census not sampling): for all 6 pairs' `d3_resolve`, independently re-derived the D3 selection by walking each pair's D1 list in (path ordinal, line) order per CONVENTIONS.md's D3 rule (first `removed`, else first non-`added` entry with real declaration-range text difference) and recomputed each `sha256` from the stated `base` blob with `sed -n 'start,endp' <file> | sed 's/\r$//' | head -c -1 | sha256sum`. Additionally (leader instruction #2): independently re-scanned all 6 pairs' full `git diff -U0` output (not just the sampled subset) with `grep -E '^[+-]\s*\[|^[+-]\s*///'` for attribute-line and XML-doc-comment changes not captured in D1, to check the author's 'zero attribute/remark changes' claim rather than trust it.

results.summary: All 54 sampled items match the corpus exactly (symbol, kind, path, line, d2Excluded/d2 membership all confirmed correct). All 6 pairs' D3 selections are the correct first-eligible-member per CONVENTIONS.md's rule (verified by walking each pair's full path-ordered D1 list by hand: DIFF-01/02/05/06 correctly skip files 1-2 of pure `added` entries and land on the first genuine `bodyChanged`; DIFF-03 correctly skips files 1-5 of pure additions and lands on the first `signatureChanged` (private->internal); DIFF-04 correctly picks the very-first-entry `removed` rename target) and all 6 `sha256` hashes were recomputed independently and match byte-for-byte. The independent re-scan of all 6 pairs' full diffs for attribute-line (`^[+-]\s*\[`) and XML-doc (`^[+-]\s*///`) changes found only: (a) attributes on brand-new (`added`-kind) declarations, already correctly excluded from needing a separate signatureChanged/remarkChanged entry since the whole declaration is new; (b) DIFF-04's 2 `[InlineData]` attribute changes, which belong to the already-modeled REMOVED+ADDED rename pair (D04-D1-01/02) per CONVENTIONS.md's rename rule, not a separate entry; (c) new `///` doc comments, individually traced to specific target lines and confirmed each one sits on a brand-new (`added`-kind) member (HeaderPage.PublicationLock, TransactionGate class, TransactionPages.HasCommitCallbacks, QueryExecutor.ExplainPlan, IndexKeyTypeWarning class, IndexKeyTypeWarning.GetFamily, DateExtensions.ToUtcDateTime), never a remark added/changed on a pre-existing member. No case of a same-name existing member's attribute or XML-doc changing alone (which would need a new signatureChanged/remarkChanged entry under the 2026-09-25 convention) was found anywhere in the 6 pairs. No corrections were made to this file's answer data; only `crossCheck`/`crossCheckPlan` fields were written, per this cross-check task's scope.
